title: Why FCEV Fits Cold-Chain Logistics
subtitle: Comparing fuel-cell and battery-electric trucks for refrigerated freight
bevAlt: Illustrative battery-electric refrigerated truck, white body with blue accents
fcevAlt: Illustrative hydrogen fuel-cell refrigerated truck, white body with blue and green accents
assetNote: Conceptual vehicle renders · not specific production models
scope: Figures describe an example cold-chain scenario; actual results depend on vehicle, load, route and infrastructure.

energy.bevCallout: Both systems draw electrical energy throughout the trip.
energy.fcevCallout: Fast hydrogen stops may help routes with sustained refrigeration demand.
energy.explanation: Refrigeration adds a continuous load to either truck. The operating advantage depends on the route and available refueling or charging.

payload.bevCallout: A large battery pack can reduce the remaining payload allowance.
payload.fcevCallout: Some fuel-cell designs may retain more cargo capacity.
payload.explanation: Payload is vehicle-specific: compare complete truck mass and axle limits before drawing a conclusion.

time.bevLabel: BEV charging in the example case
time.bevCallout: At least 1–2 hours, depending on the charging setup.
time.fcevLabel: Hydrogen refueling in the example case
time.explanation: Shorter stops may help protect delivery schedules. These are scenario figures, not guaranteed times for every truck or station.

range.bevCallout: Charging access and refrigeration demand must be included in the route plan.
range.explanation: The reported FCEV range can suit medium- and long-distance cold-chain work. The briefing material gives no comparable BEV range.
